messages.subject: Speed of display geom_hex(), geom_smooth()
parts:
I am trying to create some plots of some observation
against date of measurement. Lots of observations (500k
split across a number of treatments), so I decided to
use geom_hex() to simplify matters.

I also want to add a curve to give an indication of
what any trend over time.

Plus, break it up into facets/panels based on a treatment.

I have:

g <- ggplot(d,aes(x=date_birth,y=obs))+geom_hex()
+geom_smooth(colour="orange",method="loess",se=FALSE)
+facet_wrap(~treat,nrow=2)

On a small example, this seems to work. However, on my
actual data it takes forever (I say forever, but I mean
I haven't managed to see a graph on my screen yet).

If I exclude the geom_smooth, it is considerably quicker
when drawing to the screen - I have managed to get plots
with just the geom_hex.

Is there a quicker way to achieve what I'm trying to do?
Would it be quicker to write to a file and view them, or
will that be just as slow?

I have yet to optimise the look of my graphs and fear it
could take forever.

Ron.
